translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: Let's settle up, ferryman, if you don't mind. How much you owe me so far. That way we won't have to fight about it later.

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: Fine by me, Hermes. Better to get it sorted out. Less hassle.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: I brought you an anchor when you ordered it. Five drachmas.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: I swear by Hades, that's what I paid for it. And a rudder — two obols.

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: Put down five drachmas and two obols.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: And a needle for the sail — I paid five obols for that.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: And wax to patch the holes in your little boat, plus nails and rope — that's where you got the rigging. Two drachmas for everything.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: That's it, unless we missed something in the accounting. So when exactly are you planning to pay me back?

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: Right now? Impossible, Hermes. But if some plague or war sends us a bunch of people all at once, then I can make a profit by skimming a little off the ferry fares.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: So now I'm supposed to sit here praying for disasters just so I can get my money back?

translation.speaker: Charon
translation.text: No other way, Hermes. Right now, as you can see, we're getting hardly anyone. It's peacetime.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: I guess that's better, even if it means you keep owing me money. But you know, Charon, the old-timers who used to come down here — what men they were! All brave, most of them covered in blood and battle wounds. Now it's either someone poisoned by his boyfriend or his wife, or some guy who ate himself to death, all bloated in the belly and legs. They're all pale and pathetic — nothing like those heroes. Most of them are here because of money, plotting against each other, apparently.

translation.speaker: Hermes
translation.text: So I don't think I'm being unreasonable, demanding what you owe me.

thinking:
This dialogue is pure sitcom gold — Hermes as the put-upon creditor trying to collect from Charon, who's basically running a cash-only business with no cash flow. The itemized bill (anchor, rudder, sail needle, wax, nails, rope) reads like a hardware store receipt, which I played up with contemporary phrasing.

Charon's payment plan is classic deadbeat logic: 'I'll pay you when business picks up' — which requires people to die en masse. Hermes's exasperated response ('So now I'm supposed to sit here praying for disasters?') captures the absurdity perfectly.

The contrast between ancient heroes (bloody, brave) and modern dead (poisoned by lovers, died of gluttony) is Lucian's social commentary, but I kept it punchy rather than preachy. 'Ate himself to death, all bloated' lands the physical comedy.

Key voice choices: Hermes is frustrated but professional (he's keeping receipts), Charon is matter-of-fact about his sketchy business model. Both are comfortable with the moral implications — this is just how things work down here.
uncertainties: παραλογιζόμενον τὰ πορθμεῖα - 'skimming off the ferry fares' vs 'cheating on the fares' — went with 'skimming' as more specific to the scam
ἐξῳδηκὼς τὴν γαστέρα - literally 'swollen up the belly' but 'ate himself to death, all bloated' captures both the cause and effect
Level of contemporary slang - kept it conversational but not too slangy since they're discussing business
